REAL-WORLD REPOSITORIES

A new codebase. A real issue.

Random tasks from SWE-bench Verified (Python: Django, SymPy, scikit-learn and more) and SWE-bench Multilingual (nine other languages). Work in the historical source of established projects, with the issue brief and its regression tests.

About the task library ↗

Tasks include bug fixes and feature work. New selections avoid repeats until the matching pool is exhausted. Large environments can require several GB of disk and minutes to prepare.

Or warm up with a short incident

Real files · Failing tests · Local execution

BRING A CODEBASE

Start from GitHub

Import any public repository, including large or archived projects. Choose your own issue and configure its test command.

A 0.5B model can be wrong. Verifying its advice is part of the exercise.

Local setup

Everything runs on this computer. Two local services power practice sessions.

Ollama: the AI assistant and reviewer

Install Ollama, then download a chat model. Any installed chat model appears in the assistant's model picker. A 7–9B coding-capable model gives the most realistic experience:

ollama pull qwen3:8b

Docker Desktop: Python sandbox

Python sessions and real-world repos run in disposable containers with no network access. JavaScript sessions run inside your browser and don't need Docker.

Repo practice models

The real-world repo mode uses a deliberately small 0.5B copilot and a 3B interviewer.
